page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highmem-2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the N1 family. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core of an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 13.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 6.5 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations place the n1-highmem-2 in lower performance tiers. Single-core CPU performance via stress-ng is rated as weak, scoring 1105.58, while multi-core performance drops to the bottom 10% with a score of 1452.88. Memory bandwidth tests show 80.89 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 13.32 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, both falling into the bottom 10% tier. Geekbench testing mirrors these results, with a single-core score of 944.0 and a multi-core score of 1124.0. Database operations and Redis SET performance are also limited, with Redis achieving 1.38 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n1-highmem-2 provides a high memory allocation relative to its compute resources, making it suitable for memory-bound workloads that do not require intensive CPU throughput. However, the tradeoff is its low processing power and memory bandwidth. This instance is best suited for lightweight databases, caching layers, basic web serving, and memory-intensive background tasks that can tolerate lower CPU performance.
